tags: why do dogs love tug of war
script: The second that rope comes out, some dogs completely lose it, pulling, growling, shaking their head like they're taking down actual prey, and that reaction is older than domestication itself. Tug-of-war taps directly into predatory instinct, the pulling and resistance mimics exactly what pulling apart prey would have felt like for their wild ancestors, which is why it feels so deeply satisfying to them. That growling that makes new owners nervous is almost always play growling, a completely different sound and body posture from real aggression, loose wiggly body, relaxed face, versus a stiff body and hard stare for the real thing. Tug is also genuinely great for dogs, it burns physical energy fast, builds confidence, and when you control when the game starts and stops, it actually reinforces impulse control and your bond with them. So that intense rope battle isn't a problem to worry about, it's your dog getting to be a dog. Want more real dog behavior insight? The link's below.
